en.title: Minimum Trucks Under Total Capacity and Per-Category Limits
en.description:
Each category has items[i] packages that can be assigned independently. Each truck carries at most C packages, and at most L packages of the same category. All packages must be shipped; find the minimum number of trucks. A category does not have to ride together in a single truck. With no packages at all, 0 trucks are needed.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n C L; the second line contains the count of each category. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 0≤count≤10^9, 1≤C,L≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 4 and 4. The third example is determined by the per-truck limit for a single category.
hints: The answer is the larger of the total count divided by C rounded up and the largest category count divided by L rounded up.
